newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Digi says may be profitable in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Digi says may be profitable in Q3.

text.p: U.S.-based computer communications company Digi International Inc may return to profit in the third quarter of its fiscal year ending September 30, 1997, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"We are planning to be profitable. My commitment to the board is by the end of the fiscal year but it could be sooner in Q3," Digi president and chief executive officer Jerry Dusa told Reuters in an interview.
But Dusa said Digi would still be in the red for the full financial year.
"Because of the size of the restructuring charge, we won't be profitable for the whole year," he said.

Digi reported a loss of US$9.4 million in the second quarter ended March 31, 1997 which included a US$10.5 million restructuring charge and a US$1.6 million loss on an investment in AetherWorks Corp, a development stage company.
This was after a loss of US$2.6 million in the first quarter ended December 31, 1996, which included a loss of US$1.5 million loss in AetherWorks Corp.
Dusa said that on top of various cost cutting and consolidation measures, the company was controlling the level of shipments to its distributors which would impact on its profitability.
